ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

payload.proof_nl:
Let N := r+a+b. Since 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, we have N >= b >= a >= 0; in particular 0 <= a <= N and 0 <= b <= N, and also N-a = r+b >= 0 and N-b = r+a >= 0. By the standard polynomial form of Gaussian q-binomial coefficients, for 0 <= t <= N one has [N choose t]_q = (q;q)_N / ((q;q)_t (q;q)_{N-t}). Therefore
[N choose b]_q / [N choose a]_q = ((q;q)_N / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{N-b})) / ((q;q)_N / ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{N-a})) = ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{N-a}) / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{N-b}).
Using N-a = r+b and N-b = r+a, this becomes
[N choose b]_q / [N choose a]_q = ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b) = R_{a,b,r}(q).
Thus R_{a,b,r}(q) is exactly a quotient of two Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. By hypothesis R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q], so this quotient is a polynomial in q. Applying the allowed semantic anchor with n = N, k = b, and l = a, we conclude that every coefficient of R_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative. Since R_{a,b,r}(q) is in Z[q], all of its coefficients are integers. Therefore, for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer. This proves the lemma.
payload.role_in_assembly: This is the deep positivity input; together with reciprocity it yields full nonnegativity of all coefficients.

payload.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.

The illegality is the final positivity step, which cites the root semantic theorem statement itself. The ancestry summary explicitly marks the root theorem as forbidden citable context, so this creates a circular dependency.
